searchText: hi guys, i was trying to understand verkel construction scheme at: https://notes.ethereum.org/nrQqhVpQRi6acQckwm1Ryg?view. in f0(omeiga ^ 0bindex) is there a typeo with respect to 0b (my guess is 0x for hex) as I am unable to figure out where 0b comes from The 0b means it's in binary So those three numbers are 10, 7, 5 my other doubt is why are we reshasing the commitment H(C0), H(C1) at the inner nodes, as commitment itself is a hash. is it to map it back to same input size to pair it with a leaf at the same level of same parent? A commitment is a a 48-byte object, a value inside a polynomial has to fit into ~31.5 bytes thanks that resolves my confusion. i have another doubt regarding the next section: in this are f0, f1 polynomials at leaves (as we are talking about multi leaf eval) or they are polys from the path talked in the previous sections. So the idea of the verkle tree proof is that first you re-express it as a simple polynomial comimtment multi-proof For example, if you have a single verkle branch `A -> B -> C -> leaf` with path 1, 3, 5 You re-express that as: ``` A(1) = hash(B) B(3) = hash(C) C(5) = hash(leaf) ``` And you're trying to prove all three statements simultaneously so its the commitment of the path that we are building here right we're trying to prove the relation at every step of every path and a "verkel multiproof" is: proof of the path of all the leaves in one go r here is random because contract/account transaction/interactions here from the outsideworld i.e. the inputs is being assumed as random? there seems to be no other source of entropy. The source of entropy is the hash of all the data provided by the prover up until that point in the protocol ok understood, this is via Fiat–Shamir_heuristic. But in Fiat–Shamir_heuristic, prover has the incentive to hash a random value/salt with his secret K so as to not reveal his secret K, but here he has incentive to NOT choose a random input (input data is not really a secret here as block will have transaction/data) so as to cancel some remainders in g(X). I wonder if a rainbow attack is possible Fiat-shamir does not require the committed data to be private for security got it, but intractable discreet logarithm would be enough to make this argument that adusting r with inputs to cancel remainders in g(x) would be computationally infeasible? ( just trying to zero down my own understanding of this claim). in practice there would anyway be a proposer chosen at random (implying random state verkel trie for e.g.) in which he would be building his commitment D, which would anyway add more entropy to the scheme. You do need a random oracle assumption for the hash function for fiat shamir to work thank you, this clarifies the fiat shamir reference!
